findings.description: The instance user_data exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plain text. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or from the instance metadata service, and the keys are committed to version control.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the legacy IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF flaw in the Apache-served application could be used to retrieve instance credentials without authentication.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device configuration enables encryption, so the instance's attached storage may be created unencrypted at rest.

The instance is launched into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch and an internet gateway route, giving it a public address reachable from the internet alongside a security group that permits 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH.
The ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user data configures only plain HTTP on Apache, so all traffic to end users is unencrypted in transit.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is deliberately commented out), so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and specifies no KMS encryption, so the snapshot data — which can be shared across accounts — is stored unencrypted.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration and no KMS key, so network audit records are stored unencrypted.
The bucket defines no public access block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy denying non-TLS access, leaving sensitive flow log data at risk of unintended public or cross-account exposure.
The audit log bucket has neither versioning nor access logging configured, so tampering with or deletion of flow log evidence would be unrecoverable and untraceable.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, placing workloads that need no inbound internet access directly on the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes this a public subnet by default, so any resource launched into it is directly internet-addressable rather than isolated in a private network layer.
The VPC is created without an accompanying aws_default_security_group resource restricting its rules, so the default security group remains permissive for any resource that inherits it.
